text: Anne Morgan, Baroness Hunsdon (c. 1529 – 19 January 1607), was an English official born around 1529 at Arkestone, Herefordshire, the daughter of Sir Thomas Morgan and Anne Elizabeth Whitney, daughter of Sir James Whitney and Blanche Milbourne. The Morgan family was of Welsh origin. On 21 May 1545, she married Henry Carey, son of Sir William Carey and Mary Boleyn, the elder sister of Queen consort Anne Boleyn; due to Carey's mother having been a mistress of King Henry VIII, some, including John Hales, vicar of Isleworth, speculated that Carey was the King's illegitimate son. Henry Carey was created Baron Hunsdon on 13 January 1559, after which Anne was styled Baroness Hunsdon. Following her elevation, she served Queen Elizabeth I as a Lady of the Privy Chamber, who was also her husband's first cousin and held the couple in high favour. Carey was appointed Captain of the Gentlemen-at-Arms, serving as the Queen's personal bodyguard. A painting by an unknown artist commemorates a visit by the Queen to Anne and Carey at Hunsdon House in Hertfordshire in September 1571; Anne is believed to be depicted among the Queen's Ladies in the royal procession as the foremost lady dressed in white. Anne's portrait, painted by a follower of George Gower, is displayed at Hatfield House. The couple had thirteen children, two of whom died in infancy. Henry Carey had several illegitimate children, including Valentine Carey; one of his mistresses was Emilia Bassano, believed by some, including A. L. Rowse, to have been the inspiration for William Shakespeare's sonnet The Dark Lady, due to her black hair and dark complexion; her son Henry, born in 1592, may have been fathered by her, although she was 63 at the time of the child's birth. Upon Henry Carey's death on 23 July 1596, he left his family in debt; Queen Elizabeth I paid for his funeral expenses, gave Anne a gift of £400, and provided her with an annual pension of £200 from the Exchequer. Anne used part of the funds to erect a monument to her husband in Westminster Abbey. On 14 December 1595, seven months before Carey's death, Queen Elizabeth appointed Anne as Keeper of Somerset House, a royal residence where the Queen had lived before her accession; Anne held this post for life, having previously held it in 1574 with her husband. Anne died on 19 January 1607 and was buried in Westminster Abbey; her will, dated 10 January 1607, was proved on 22 January.
